findings.reason: the §27 worker would either leave an added failure it is told not to repair (failing its own done-when and blocking promotion) or edit a case its brief forbids, so the case list or the "no other case … changes" clause must change before dispatch.
findings.text: the section's write paths name only three cases in this file (`test_a_moved_ledger_is_read_against`, `test_two_picks_read_each_foreign_ledger_once`, `test_a_fresh_process_with_no_records_reads_no_ledger`) and declare "no other case in those files changes", but `test_the_persisted_cache_prefers_reckon_home` calls `lane_context._cached_run_time_profile("cache-order-probe", now=NOW)` (line 75) and then asserts the cache entry was written under `RECKON_HOME` and not under `XDG_CACHE_HOME` (`.is_file()` at line 79) — that is the pick-time *persistence* the deliverable removes when it states "A pick never calls `run_time_profile`" and moves "Rebuilding … off the pick" onto the refresh function, so under §27 no entry is written by the pick and the assertion fails; the case therefore must change but the write-paths clause forbids changing it and the done-when ("no added failure against the base revision") cannot be met as written

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves: `_cached_run_time_profile`, `_expected_wait`, `local_lane` (`reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py`), `cached_pick_input_rekeyed`, `_read_pick_entry`, `reckon/capabilities.py:1226,1285,1314`), the §25 document (`docs/research/the-pick-state-render-is-slow-because.html`), and all five named test cases (`tests/test_picker_foreign_wait_is_bounded.py:127,83,294`; `tests/test_dispatch_speed.py:698,763`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the node's done-when measures "no added failure" for the test files importing `lane_context.py`, but the write-paths sentence added in this unit enumerates only five cases in the two files and forbids any other case from changing, while a sixth case in one of those files asserts the very pick-time write the section removes.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the measure is a test in the repository and a promotion-path test; no gate log is placed on a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the added write paths name test files and case names only; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches code, and `§25`/`§27` appear in plan prose alone.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause (a promotion moves a project's ledger stamp, so the next pick rebuilds that project's 14-day profile synchronously inside `pick()`) matches §25's cited join, the stated read path is real (`cached_pick_input_rekeyed` at `reckon/capabilities.py:1314` returns a stored value only when `entry["key"]` equals the current stamp, which is why the moved-stamp read must go through `_read_pick_entry`), and both the promotion caller and the pick-side read are named.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the serve-or-none read, the promotion-triggered refresh that replaces the removed rebuild, and the new `expected_wait_profile_age_s` field are one mechanism and its observable, reviewable on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §27's `depends-on` (`lane-and-model-routing#s25`, `jev-learns-from-its-routes#s5`) both resolve to sections that exist and are landed/declared, and followup `f-lmr-015` sequences the dispatch after the `jev-learns-from-its-routes` §5 node (`docs/plans/jev-learns-from-its-routes.html` has a declared `id="s5"`).
